Here is a concise factual research note on the candidate news item ("World's First Electric Plane Successfully Flies Carrying 19 Passengers"), based on verified sources.  

---

## Summary of What Actually Happened

### What occurred

- On **14 November 2026**, China’s aerospace manufacturer **COMAC** flew its prototype electric aircraft, the **CE-25A**, in a **first crewed flight test** at Binzhou, Shandong province. ([cnnindonesia.com](https://www.cnnindonesia.com/gaya-hidup/20261118205459-269-1428733/pesawat-komersial-listrik-china-terbang-perdana-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  
- On board were **two pilots** and **one flight-test engineer (technician)**. ([inet.detik.com](https://inet.detik.com/cyberlife/d-8754563/china-sukses-terbangkan-pesawat-listrik-bisa-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  
- The aircraft was airborne for **16 minutes and 38 seconds**, covering about **60.4 kilometers** during that crewed flight. ([inet.detik.com](https://inet.detik.com/cyberlife/d-8754563/china-sukses-terbangkan-pesawat-listrik-bisa-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  

### Key specifications & design claims

- The CE-25A is designed to carry **19 passengers**, but the test flight did **not** include any passengers beyond crew. ([indianexpress.com](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/china-10-tonne-electric-commercial-aircraft-first-piloted-flight-explained-10969641/lite/?utm_source=openai))  
- Maximum takeoff weight is about **10 metric tons** (≈22,000 lb). ([newatlas.com](https://newatlas.com/aircraft/comac-ce-25a-electric-airliner-first-crewed-flight?utm_source=openai))  
- Claimed cruise speed: **300 km/h** (≈186 mph). Claimed service ceiling: **2,400 meters** above sea level. ([cnbcindonesia.com](https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/tech/20261117062349-37-785775/pesawat-listrik-buatan-china-terbang-perdana-kapasitas-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  
- Claimed maximum range (under design goals) is **400 kilometers**. ([cnbcindonesia.com](https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/tech/20261117062349-37-785775/pesawat-listrik-buatan-china-terbang-perdana-kapasitas-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  

### Certification and operational status

- COMAC has **applied** to China’s aviation regulator, the **Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC)**, for a **type certificate**. This is a regulatory step but **does not imply** that commercial passenger operations have been approved or started. ([newatlas.com](https://newatlas.com/aircraft/comac-ce-25a-electric-airliner-first-crewed-flight?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Comparison with the Candidate’s Claim

| Claim in Candidate | Verification / Correction |
|---|---|
| The first electric plane successfully flew carrying **19 passengers**. | **False**. The CE-25A is *designed* to carry 19 passengers, but the actual crewed flight included **no paying or test passengers**—only crew (two pilots + one engineer). ([inet.detik.com](https://inet.detik.com/cyberlife/d-8754563/china-sukses-terbangkan-pesawat-listrik-bisa-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai)) |
| Date: 2026-11-20, Country: Indonesia. | Partially incorrect. The event actually took place on **14 November 2026** in **China**, not Indonesia. ([cnnindonesia.com](https://www.cnnindonesia.com/gaya-hidup/20261118205459-269-1428733/pesawat-komersial-listrik-china-terbang-perdana-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai)) |

---

## Independent / Primary Sources

- **Primary sources**:  
  - COMAC’s statements (via Chinese state media) reported through outlets like Xinhua. ([cnnindonesia.com](https://www.cnnindonesia.com/internasional/20261116151333-106-1427703/china-sukses-uji-terbang-pesawat-listrik-bisa-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  
  - Official reports about the test flight published by international tech and aviation media (e.g., *The Indian Express*, *Business Today*) quoting specifications and flight-test results. ([indianexpress.com](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/china-10-tonne-electric-commercial-aircraft-first-piloted-flight-explained-10969641/lite/?utm_source=openai))  

- **Independent sources**:  
  - News outlets such as CNN Indonesia and CNBC Indonesia that reproduced the event and details. ([inet.detik.com](https://inet.detik.com/cyberlife/d-8754563/china-sukses-terbangkan-pesawat-listrik-bisa-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  
  - Aviation-technology focused press (New Atlas, etc.) that analyze the event, verify details, and caution that the passenger-carrying capacity is design intent rather than demonstrated. ([newatlas.com](https://newatlas.com/aircraft/comac-ce-25a-electric-airliner-first-crewed-flight?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Completed/Measured Outcomes vs Announcements and Plans

- **Completed / Measured outcomes**:  
  - A successful first crewed flight (on 14 Nov 2026) with crew onboard flying 60.4 km for 16:38. ([inet.detik.com](https://inet.detik.com/cyberlife/d-8754563/china-sukses-terbangkan-pesawat-listrik-bisa-angkut-19-penumpang?utm_source=openai))  

- **Announcements / Plans / Claims**, not yet realized:  
  - For 19 passenger capacity: this is design capacity, not demonstrated in flight. ([indianexpress.com](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/china-10-tonne-electric-commercial-aircraft-first-piloted-flight-explained-10969641/lite/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Operation over full 400 km range, commercial service, or certification: still pending. ([newatlas.com](https://newatlas.com/aircraft/comac-ce-25a-electric-airliner-first-crewed-flight?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Research Note Summary

- The **claim** that a world-first electric plane has *successfully flown carrying 19 passengers* is **not supported** by reliable sources. The prototype **CE-25A** is **designed** to carry 19 passengers, but its **first crewed flight** carried **only crew**, not passengers.  
- The event took place in **China** on **14 November 2026**, not in Indonesia.  
- While several specifications and design goals are claimed (range, speed, altitude), these remain **unproven** in full operational conditions.  
- Certification application to regulator has been submitted, but no commercial authorization yet.  

---

If you want, I can track future developments to see when the CE-25A begins commercial operations or carries paying passengers, to see whether the “19-passenger” claim becomes a demonstrated outcome.

stories.research_notes:
Here is what I found by searching for the candidate story “Earlier Preoperative Lung Exercise Aids Postoperative Recovery in Elderly Cancer Surgery.” There is strong evidence that such outcomes are real, although the specific headline seems to be a variation or summary drawing on recent studies rather than a single named article. Below are the verified findings and data from primary research, plus notes on what has *not* yet been established.

---

## What Actually Happened

Recent peer-reviewed studies have found that **starting pulmonary (lung) exercise before surgery**, particularly in elderly lung cancer patients, is associated with measurable postoperative benefits. Key findings include:

- **Retrospective study (Shanghai, China)**: In patients aged elderly (criteria ≥ age not specified here), initiating pulmonary exercise *at the time of surgical decision in outpatient clinic* (versus beginning at hospital admission) resulted in **better pulmonary function** one day before surgery *and* three months after, **shorter postoperative hospital stays**, and **lower rates of complications**. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13019-026-04771-w?utm_source=openai))  
- **Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs)**: Across 1,129 patients, prehabilitation including exercise improved six-minute walk distance (average increase ~37.6 m), reduced postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs), and shortened length of hospital stay (LOS). ([jtd.amegroups.org](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/120260/html?utm_source=openai))  
- **Multicentre RCT for high-risk patients undergoing lung resection**: A 14-day multimodal prehabilitation program (high-intensity respiratory muscle training + nutritional support + smoking cessation + psychological support) significantly **reduced PPCs** (from ~55% in usual care to ~34% in prehabilitation) and reduced hospital stay (median from 9 to 7 days). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12597589/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Completed / Measured Outcomes vs. Announcements

The following are outcomes measured and confirmed in clinical studies, *not* just pledges or preliminary plans:

- Improvements in preoperative pulmonary function metrics (e.g., forced expiratory volume, forced vital capacity, peak expiratory flow). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13231665/?utm_source=openai))  
- Reduction in postoperative complications (especially pulmonary complications). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12597589/?utm_source=openai))  
- Shorter lengths of postoperative or total hospital stay. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12597589/?utm_source=openai))  
- Enhanced functional exercise capacity preoperatively (e.g. 6-minute walk distance). ([jtd.amegroups.org](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/120260/html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What Is *Less* Certain or Not Yet Verified

- **“Earlier”** as in *clinic-decision time vs admission* is supported by that one recent retrospective study. It is not yet established which precise lead time is best for every patient. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13019-026-04771-w?utm_source=openai))  
- Many studies focused on short-term outcomes (up to a few weeks or months postoperative); long-term functional recovery beyond a few months is less well-documented. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6751530/?utm_source=openai))  
- The headline “elderly cancer surgery” is often more specifically “elderly lung cancer surgery (thoracic, lung resection)”—other cancer types have less strong evidence. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37442190/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Evidence Quality & Independent Confirmation

- The findings are supported by multiple independent trials and meta-analyses. For example, the multicentre RCT and the systematic meta-analysis are independent of each other. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12597589/?utm_source=openai))  
- The retrospective study adds support to the idea that *timing* of preoperative exercise matters. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13019-026-04771-w?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Concrete Figures & Dates

- The **retrospective study** included 152 elderly lung cancer patients in 2024. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13019-026-04771-w?utm_source=openai))  
- In the multicentre RCT (prehabilitation vs usual care), in patients aged about 64–75 years old, complications dropped from 55% to 34%, and hospital stay reduced from 9 to 7 days. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12597589/?utm_source=openai))  
- In the systematic review/meta-analysis up to December 2025, the increase in 6MWD was ~37.58 m on average. ([jtd.amegroups.org](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/120260/html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Relation to the Candidate Headline

- The candidate headline (“Earlier Preoperative Lung Exercise Aids Postoperative Recovery in Elderly Cancer Surgery”) accurately reflects core findings from multiple recent studies, especially the retrospective one about earlier initiation and the meta-analysis generalizing benefits.
- There is no indication yet that a *single new study published exactly on November 20, 2026* matches that headline verbatim. The most recent relevant primary article is the retrospective study published October 30, 2026. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13019-026-04771-w?utm_source=openai))  

---

Let me know if you’d like tracking of specific statistics (e.g. by age group, amount of lead time) or a comparison to similar interventions in non-lung cancer surgeries.

stories.research_notes:
Here is a research note on the event “Rescue of over 90 people during floods in Hollywood, demonstrating significant community action”.

---

### What Actually Happened

**Event:**  
Heavy rains in Broward County, Florida (including Hollywood) caused severe flooding, leading to rescues, evacuations, property damage, and a declaration of a state of emergency.

---

### Key Facts & Figures

- Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) officers were involved in rescue operations including evacuations, welfare checks, and transporting people for medical assistance. ([tampabay28.com](https://www.tampabay28.com/news/state/fwc-officers-rescue-infant-and-disabled-veteran-amid-south-florida-flooding?utm_source=openai))  
- In Broward County, over **90 residents** were **evacuated, rescued, or transported** from a flooded apartment complex. ([tampabay28.com](https://www.tampabay28.com/news/state/fwc-officers-rescue-infant-and-disabled-veteran-amid-south-florida-flooding?utm_source=openai))  
- Among those rescued were an **infant** who had stopped breathing when a vehicle got stuck in floodwaters, and a **disabled veteran** whose wheelchair was swept away. ([tampabay28.com](https://www.tampabay28.com/news/state/fwc-officers-rescue-infant-and-disabled-veteran-amid-south-florida-flooding?utm_source=openai))  
- In one apartment complex (La Vue at Emerald Pointe in Hollywood), more than **70 residents** and **20–30 pets** were rescued. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/hollywood-flooded-apartment-complex-fwc-rescues-la-vue-emerald-pointe-nov-18-2026/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Completion / Measured Outcome vs Plans

- This was not just an announcement or plan: **the rescue operations were carried out**, meaning the outcome (over 90 people helped) was measured and completed.  
- There were **no reported deaths or serious injuries** among those rescued from the apartment complex. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/hollywood-flooded-apartment-complex-fwc-rescues-la-vue-emerald-pointe-nov-18-2026/?utm_source=openai))  
- Damage included water intrusion into first-floor units, many vehicles damaged or “totaled,” and disruption of daily life, such as school closures. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/hollywood-flooded-apartment-complex-fwc-rescues-la-vue-emerald-pointe-nov-18-2026/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Sources

**Original or primary source:**

- MyFWC (Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission) official account of rescue operations—this includes numbers of officers deployed, equipment used, and details about specific rescues (infant, disabled veteran). ([tampabay28.com](https://www.tampabay28.com/news/state/fwc-officers-rescue-infant-and-disabled-veteran-amid-south-florida-flooding?utm_source=openai))  

**Independent coverage:**

- CBS News Miami reported the rescue of over 70 residents and 20–30 pets from the flooded Hollywood apartment complex. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/hollywood-flooded-apartment-complex-fwc-rescues-la-vue-emerald-pointe-nov-18-2026/?utm_source=openai))  
- NBC Miami reported the broader flooding event, including nearly 90 calls for service by fire rescue and police, shelter activation, and streets under water. ([nbcmiami.com](https://www.nbcmiami.com/weather/stories-weather/families-rescued-neighborhoods-underwater-in-hollywood-after-historic-flooding/3890250/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Clarifications & Context

- The incident took place amid a multi-day heavy rainfall event affecting South Florida, particularly Broward County. ([wsvn.com](https://wsvn.com/news/local/miami-dade/storms-cause-extensive-flooding-in-broward-hollywood-declares-state-of-emergency/?utm_source=openai))  
- Hollywood, Florida (Broward County) declared a **state of emergency** in response to the flooding. ([wsvn.com](https://wsvn.com/news/local/miami-dade/storms-cause-extensive-flooding-in-broward-hollywood-declares-state-of-emergency/?utm_source=openai))  
- Roof collapse was reported at Temple Sinai synagogue in Hollywood due to rain. No injuries reported. ([wsvn.com](https://wsvn.com/news/local/miami-dade/storms-cause-extensive-flooding-in-broward-hollywood-declares-state-of-emergency/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Comparison with Candidate Headline

- The candidate headline states: “Rescue of over 90 people during floods in Hollywood, demonstrating significant community action.”  
- That is **mostly accurate**: over 90 people were *evacuated, rescued, or transported for medical assistance* by FWC officers. ([tampabay28.com](https://www.tampabay28.com/news/state/fwc-officers-rescue-infant-and-disabled-veteran-amid-south-florida-flooding?utm_source=openai))  
- However, in one specific building (La Vue), the number is more tightly “over 70 residents” plus pets. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/hollywood-flooded-apartment-complex-fwc-rescues-la-vue-emerald-pointe-nov-18-2026/?utm_source=openai))  
- "Over 90" applies to the broader set of rescue/evacuation/transport operations by FWC in Broward, not just one complex. ([tampabay28.com](https://www.tampabay28.com/news/state/fwc-officers-rescue-infant-and-disabled-veteran-amid-south-florida-flooding?utm_source=openai))  

---

If you like, I can track down the exact locations, timing, and any longer-term consequences of the flooding.
